decisions.reason: Product A is a home-page flagship closely tied to the firm's direction with high visible commitment, so escalation pressures make dropping it very unlikely.
Although not a flagship, Product B builds on the established offer and has its own public page, so prior investment and public commitment support keeping it.
As a recent launch building on established capabilities with its own page, any disappointing results can still be attributed to temporary causes, favoring persistence.
Because Product D is distant from the established offer and less central, it has a higher drop risk, but the recent public launch and sunk costs still make keeping more likely.
Similar to D, Product E's distance from core and less central public commitment raise the probability of dropping, yet the recent launch and public presence favor keeping under escalation.
Product F is a flagship product line central to the announced direction with high public commitment, so escalation strongly favors keeping it.
